content.comment_body: Hello, here’s an example of communication with [version_no]. See [url]. [product_name] acting as server writes data to [version_no] tags, which works fine. Plenty of examples can be found on YouTube. However, when [product_name] acts as client and tries to receive data from [version_no], it doesn’t work. Does anyone have instructions on performing PUT/GET communication with [version_no]? Thanks, [user_name]
Hello [user_name], have you tried unchecking the "Establish active connection" option in the engineering tool? For me, that solved a similar problem.

Hello, that setting only helps if [product_name] writes data to [version_no]. I need to read and write data from [version_no] to [product_name], so I have to use the PUT/GET instruction. The connection from [version_no] is established, but the instruction isn’t working.

Hello [user_name], for my project I just used an application example from [company_name]. I read an analog value from [product_name] to [version_no] and controlled two outputs of [product_name] via [version_no].
Also, Modbus should be an option. See [url] for reference.

Please review the attached GIF video. It demonstrates a connection between [version_no] and [product_name] bidirectionally. There’s no active program running in [version_no], but [product_name] is processing a number. The PDF shared by [user_name] was useful for setting up the configurations, though [version_no]’s setup deviates slightly. It’s important to grant permission for PUT and GET in the security settings; otherwise, communication won’t work. The relevant tags were given access. For [product_name], the configuration is different: using network view, you place both devices and set up data exchange with network input/output blocks, as the video shows. [user_name], does the video result match what you’re aiming for?

Hello, thanks everyone, but I need to write data from [version_no] to [product_name] only once (for configuration purposes). The existing example sends or reads data cyclically from [product_name], which works fine. It doesn’t seem possible to read configuration data, like gain values or counter settings, in [product_name] by reading cyclically before disconnecting—after disconnect, [product_name] reads null. That’s my problem: I have to write the data a single time using [product_name].

Hello, thanks for clarifying your goal. It’s understandable. What about a workaround? Try sending two values: one for the configuration value, and another bit field indicating its type. A simple approach would have `value2 = 1` signal to [product_name] that `value1` should be used; expanding this could allow up to 16 different settings. The German-language forum might have additional ideas, as many experienced users are willing to share solutions. Alternatively, you can submit a formal support request via the button on this page. Regards.
I found a helpful YouTube video; here’s the link: [url].

Hello, that’s a good video—well made and detailed. Thanks, [user_name]. It doesn’t show specifically how [version_no] can send a value just once instead of continuously; the aim should be to occupy the network only when necessary. This is a solution needed on the [version_no] side. Maybe using TCON and TDISCON instructions on [version_no] will help? You might want to ask in a dedicated communications forum that focuses on [version_no].

Hello, that’s how it works: you need to have active connection establishment checked. In the engineering portal, use GET or PUT blocks and the DB block 1 data address. The DBX address should match the variable’s location in [product_name].
Congratulations on sticking with the issue until you found a solution. Thank you for sharing your experience.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users have difficulty with writing configuration data only once from [version_no] to [product_name]. Cyclic data transfer works reliably, but single-event communication (using PUT/GET) does not deliver the desired result. Discussions show confusion about documentation, settings in the engineering tool, and actual implementation of non-cyclic writing. Clear guidance for one-time, persistent data transfer is lacking.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants to send configuration data from [version_no] to [product_name] a single time so that [product_name] retains the value even after disconnecting, thereby avoiding reliance on cyclic data transfer.
